history.summary: CSV CORRECTION: 'Shyamrai Temple, Bishnupur, Manipur' is documented as the Shyam Rai Temple at Bishnupur, BANKURA district, WEST BENGAL - the CSV's state (Manipur) is wrong; this is the famous Pancha-ratna terracotta monument, not a Manipur shrine. DUPLICATE CROSS-REF: 'Shyamrai' is the same temple as seq 645 'Pancha Ratna Temple' in this batch - the two CSV rows describe the SAME monument; consider merging or removing one. Built in 1643 AD by Malla King Raghunath Singha (son of Bir Hambir/Dhir Hambir). The finest surviving Pancha-ratna (five-spired) temple of Bengal: brick-built on a low square plinth with an ambulatory pathway and a three-arched porch on each side; the central shikhara is octagonal, the other four square. Walls are profusely decorated with terracotta carvings depicting Krishna-lila (including a large Raschakra/Rasamandala), the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and scenes of contemporary social life; the curved roof and eaves show Islamic-influenced Bengali hut (Chala) architecture. Maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India and set in a landscaped garden; a single ticket from Rasmancha covers this temple, Rasmancha and Jor Bangla.

name: Shyamrai Temple
town_description: Bishnupur in Bankura district, West Bengal, was the capital of the Malla dynasty from the 8th century and is famous as Bengal's terracotta temple town - Rasmancha (c.1600), Jor Bangla (1655), Shyam Rai/Pancharatna (1643), Madan Mohan and others. The town is also home to the Bishnupur Gharana of Hindustani classical music, Baluchari silk weaving, and the famous Bankura terracotta horse. Not to be confused with Bishnupur, Manipur.
tradition: Vaishnavism (Gaudiya Vaishnavism, which the Malla kings embraced in the 16th century; dedicated to Radha-Krishna)
